job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today in our geography class, I learned so much about our neighborhood in space. Our teacher explained that the Sun is actually a massive star at the center, not a planet, because it generates its own heat and light. We also looked at how the eight planets travel around the Sun in elliptical paths, which means their distance from the Sun changes slightly throughout their journey. It is fascinating to think that Earth is the only planet in our system known to support life because of its perfect distance from the Sun and the presence of water and air. Later, we discussed the Moon, which is our planet's only natural satellite. I used to think it glowed like a bulb, but I learned that the Moon does not produce its own light. Instead, it simply reflects the light coming from the Sun, which is why it appears to change shape in the night sky. I also learned that asteroids and meteoroids are just rocky debris floating in space, unlike the major planets that follow these specific, non-circular orbits. It makes me realize how special and unique our home planet really is in this vast, dark solar system.

Because it has no water or air
